MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 23, 2019

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ at 7:03 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Los Hermanos Royal Blue 2022 members Will Deley and Garrett Lamm led the Pledge of
Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Members Absent:  Mitchell

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Director of Community Development/Public Works David Wahba
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council.
  There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote.
  (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ recommended that consideration of Items 5B (City Council
  Minutes of June 25, 2019) and 5C (City Council Adjourned Minutes of July 8, 2019) be
  tabled until the next meeting of the COUNCIL since she and COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN will abstain from voting on those two items because they were not at the
  meetings; and that will leave no quorum to vote on items.

  There being no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN requested that Item 5I (Commission/Committee
  Attendance) be removed for individual consideration.

  There being no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JULY 23, 2019
   MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A AND D-H
  AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS JUNE AND JULY 2019

  APPROVED WARRANTS 61631 THROUGH 61723 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $921,959.62; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 060419 THROUGH 060519;
  062619; 070119 THROUGH 070419; AND 61661 (VOID) IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $589,972.57 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $1,511,932.19 WITH PROPER
  AUDIT

E.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT JUNE 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

F.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT JUNE 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF JUNE 24, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

H.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 1, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION:

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 25, 2019

  TABLED (NO QUORUM)

C.  CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED MINUTES OF JULY 8, 2019

  TABLED (NO QUORUM)

I.  COMMISSION/COMMITTEE ATTENDANCE REPORT

  Recommendation: Receive and file.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that one member of the Equestrian Committee
  has missed nearly every meeting this year and asked if there is anything that can be done.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JULY 23, 2019
   COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Equestrian Committee Chair noted that the member missed
  the last meeting because she was ill, but attends a lot of out of town equestrian events which
  cause her to miss meetings often and it may make sense to replace her.

  City Manager Grammer noted that committee members serve a one year term expiring in
  December of each year with the recruitment process beginning in September so it may make
  sense to assess the situation and take any desired action at that time.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL RECEIVE AND FILE THE COMMISSION/COMMITTEE
  ATTENDANCE REPORT

  There being no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Cal Fekete, 5 Bridlewood Circle addressed the City Council to express concern regarding the status
of the repairs to the bridle trail along Palos Verdes Drive East and the recent increases in Waste
Management’s manure collection rates.

In response to Mr. Fekete’s concerns, City Manager Grammer stated that the City Council recently
approved a contract for the PVDE storm drain repair project for completion this summer. Assistant
City Manager Davis explained the background and possible remedies related to manure collection
rates stating that staff will remain in contact with the Feketes concerning the rates.

Korey Bradbury, Cal Water provided a construction update on the Palos Verdes Peninsula Water
Reliability Project.

In response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ’s inquiry regarding the intervals for generator testing,
Mr. Bradbury stated that regular testing typically takes place during daytime hours approximately
once per month.

PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN CITIES OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES (RHE) AND RANCHO PALOS VERDES (RPV) TO JOIN RPV’S REPAVEMENT
  PROJECT AT WHITLEY COLLINS DRIVE AND NEIGHBORHOOD VICINITY

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JULY 23, 2019
   Recommendation: That the City Council enter into a Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) with the City of Rancho Palos Verdes (RPV) to participate in RPV’s resurfacing
  project to repave our portions of streets located in the Mesa Palos Verdes neighborhood
  (Quailwood Drive, Scottwood Drive, Stonecrest Road and Whitley Collins Drive) for a cost
  not to exceed $199,781.

  Director of Community Development/Public Works Wahba provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Director of Community Development/Public
  Works Wahba stated that the streets included in the project are in poor condition and
  recommended for resurfacing in the City’s Pavement Management System.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ENTERING INTO A MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE CITY OF RANCHO PALOS VERDES (RPV) TO
  PARTICIPATE IN RPV’S RESURFACING PROJECT TO REPAVE OUR
  PORTIONS OF STREETS LOCATED IN THE MESA PALOS VERDES
  NEIGHBORHOOD  (QUAILWOOD  DRIVE,  SCOTTWOOD  DRIVE,
  STONECREST ROAD AND WHITLEY COLLINS DRIVE) FOR A COST NOT TO
  EXCEED $199,781.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

OLD BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR USE OF PALOS VERDES PENINSULA
  HIGH SCHOOL SWIMMING POOL AND REVISED RENTAL FEES

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into the attached revised Memorandum of
  Understanding between Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District and the cities of
  Rolling Hills Estates and Rancho Palos Verdes for Use of Pool Facilities at Palos Verdes
  Peninsula High School beginning June 1, 2019 and ending May 30, 2024.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that in Section 4 on page 1 of the MOU, the language
  regarding the rate is confusingly worded and implies a rate of $12.50 per hour. Assistant
  City Manager Davis noted the ambiguity but confirmed that the non-profit rate is $25 per
  hour with the normal rate being $50 per hour.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, expressed concern regarding the language included
  in several sections of the MOU regarding availability of the pool facilities for City-
  sponsored summer swim programs specifically, the use of the term “reasonable efforts”.
  He also questioned the fee, noting that in discussion with the School District the City was

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JULY 23, 2019
   supposed to be charged a rate based cost recovery and suggested that it be verified that
  the rate is just recovering the cost for operating the facility during City use and does not
  include any additional fees.

  City Attorney Davis noted that when the MOU was being drafted, he recommended some
  changes to the language, but those changes were not incorporated into the final MOU.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ commented that she is concerned that if the MOU is
  approved as is, it will set a precedent for future MOUs and the language should be
  accurate now.

  Discussion ensued concerning the intent of all three parties regarding the rate for use of
  the facilities and the language regarding availability of the facilities.

  CONSIDERATION OF THIS ITEM WAS TABLED AND STAFF WAS DIRECTED
  TO WORK WITH RPV AND PVPUSD TO CLARIFY SECTION 2, 3 AND 5
  REGARDING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE FACILITY FOR CITY PROGRAMS
  AND SECTION 4 REGARDING THE RATE FOR USE OF THE FACILITY FOR
  CITY PROGRAMS.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis reported that his office is working with staff to clarify and document the
procedures for use of City facilities for non-City sponsored events.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the California JPIA (Authority)
Annual Board of Directors meeting last week, noting that some of the business items included
electing a new Executive Board; approving a new policy suggested by the Authority’s auditor
whereby the budget will be approved by the entire Board of Directors as opposed to the Executive
Board; and updating the Authority’s investment policy to include more diversified options through
development of a Captive Insurance Entity.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Equestrian Committee met on Monday night and one
of the items before the Committee was a proposal for a mounted shooting event at Ernie Howlett
Park. She noted that the Committee will be taking a field trip to see a demonstration before making
a recommendation for Park and Activities Commission and City Council consideration.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported the Neighborhood Council met last week and heard a
presentation on disaster response plans and the role amateur radio operators play in an effective
plan.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reminded those present and watching of the following upcoming
events: CERT AfterShock Chat on Thursday, July 25, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber
and National Night Out scheduled at various neighborhoods in the community on Tuesday, August
6, 2019.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JULY 23, 2019
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN informed those present and watching that Theater Friends and
the Boys & Girls Club of Los Angeles will be presenting a Theater Showcase featuring Disney’s
“Moana” on July 29, 2019 at 4:00 p.m. in San Pedro.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked staff for their efforts in putting on another successful Tracy
Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament and Tracy Austin

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently pending
  projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration and/or make
  announcements of interest to the public.

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES’ ANNUAL
  CONFERENCE AND EXPO IN LONG BEACH, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 16-18, 2019

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ALL INTERESTED COUNCIL
  MEMBERS TO ATTEND THE LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES’ ANNUAL
  CONFERENCE AND EXPO.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA JPIA RISK MANAGEMENT
  EDUCATIONAL FORUM IN INDIAN WELLS, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 9-11, 2018

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ALL INTERESTED COUNCIL
  MEMBERS TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA JPIA RISK MANAGEMENT
  EDUCATIONAL FORUM.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ so ordered.

OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ reminded those present and watching about the City’s upcoming
38th Annual Hills Are Alive 5k/10k Race scheduled for Saturday, August 10, 2019 at Ernie Howlett
Park and encourage families to participate in this fun community event.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JULY 23, 2019
 ADJOURNMENT

At 8:08 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the next
regular City Council meeting scheduled to be held on Tuesday, August 13, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in
the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling
Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Greg Grammer
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
JULY 23, 2019
